description: Labelled Game Master cases built from the extended showcase script: each scene in full (condition met) and a negative control cut before the agreement (not met). Rebuild with `pnpm gm-eval --build tests/gm-cases`.

scene.title: Team huddle
scene.goal: Agree the team's position before replying to the client

cases.condition: the team has stated a single agreed position on the request

dialogue.text: Okay, Priya's email is in. She wants a reconciliation module before go-live and an answer by end of day Friday. First reactions?
My worry is the ingestion layer. We are still hardening it, and anything we add now competes with go-live.
I would rather not say no outright. The renewal is in play, and a flat refusal will land badly.
So not a flat yes and not a flat no. What if we offer it as a phase two after go-live, scoped and priced?
I can live with that. A phased version is roughly half the work and keeps the go-live date safe.
Agreed. Position for the call: phase two after go-live, priced as a change request, with the risk to the date spelled out for her.

scene.title: Call with Priya
scene.goal: Respond to the request and agree next steps

cases.condition: a concrete next step has been agreed between the team and Priya

dialogue.text: Hi Priya, thanks for making time. We read your email and we want to help Finance tie out the daily loads.
Thanks for jumping on. I will be direct: Finance needs that reconciliation module before go-live. Can you confirm it today?
We can deliver it, but not safely before go-live. The ingestion layer is still being hardened, so we would propose a phased module right after launch.
Right after launch is not what I asked for. Walk me through the risk, because I have to explain this upstairs.

Adding new code to ingestion now puts the launch date at risk, and a late launch costs you far more than a short wait for the module. We would price the phased module separately so you can see exactly what it costs.
Okay, that is a clear argument. If it goes after launch, how soon, and what happens to Finance in the meantime?
Within three weeks of go-live. In the meantime we give Finance a manual tie-out report so nothing is blind.
Fine, I can work with three weeks if the numbers hold. Put it in writing and I will take it to my CFO, who will want to talk to you.

scene.title: Internal huddle
scene.goal: Turn the phased idea into a plan with a date, a price and a presenter

cases.condition: the team has agreed a phased plan with a date and a price to propose

dialogue.text: Priya was reasonable, but she is taking this to her CFO, so we need numbers that stand up. Tech lead, what is the honest effort for a phased module?

The phased version is about three person-weeks of build, so two engineers for a week and a half after go-live. The full module would be about six. I also want a risk review before we touch ingestion, so call it ready three weeks after launch.

Then I propose a fixed fee of 48 thousand for the phased module, delivered three weeks after go-live. I will present it to the CFO and the delivery lead owns the timeline. Are we all happy with that plan?
Yes, I am happy with that. I will own the timeline, so three weeks after go-live is a commitment from me.
I agree. Three weeks after go-live leaves room for the risk review, and 48 thousand fixed covers the build.
Good, then it is agreed: the phased module, 48 thousand fixed, three weeks after go-live, and I present it to the CFO.

scene.title: Escalation call with Priya and the CFO
scene.goal: Present the phased proposal and learn what the CFO needs in order to accept it

cases.condition: the CFO has heard the priced phased proposal and has said what she needs in order to accept it

dialogue.text: Thanks both. To recap: we propose a phased reconciliation module, delivered three weeks after go-live, so the launch date stays safe.
Helena, this is the phased option I mentioned. It gets Finance the module, just not on day one.
I have one question before adjectives: what does it cost in total, and is that a fixed price or an estimate?
It is a fixed fee of 48 thousand, separate from the programme fee, delivered three weeks after go-live.
That is higher than I hoped, but it is at least a number. Helena?
48 thousand for a module that was in an early draft and removed before signature. Why should we pay for work that was once scoped?

It was removed to protect the launch date. Building the full module now would take about six person-weeks, and doing that inside the launch window could put go-live at risk, which would cost you far more.
Helena, that matches what I was told: the ingestion work is the bottleneck.
Risk I understand. Show me what I get for the money: scope, acceptance criteria, and what happens if you miss the date.
Scope is daily tie-out of every load against the source, an exceptions report and a sign-off test with Finance. If we miss three weeks after go-live, we credit the fee proportionally.
A credit for lateness is useful. I can defend that upstairs.
A credit clause helps, but 48 thousand is still above what I expected. I need a number I can defend before the end of this call, so let us talk terms.

scene.title: Negotiating the final terms
scene.goal: Agree scope, price, date and conditions with Priya and the CFO

cases.condition: the team, Priya and the CFO have agreed final terms covering scope, delivery date and price

dialogue.text: Helena, we heard you on price. We can bring the fixed fee to 45 thousand, with delivery three weeks after go-live.
That helps me. Helena, is 45 workable?
Closer. Before I agree: is 45 firm, with no extras, and who signs the change request on your side?
It is firm. No time and materials. The change request is signed by me and by the account lead, and the credit applies if we miss the date.
Good. That is the clarity I needed for my own approval.
A firm fee and a credit clause I can accept in principle. I also want acceptance tied to Finance signing off the daily tie-out, not to your own test.
Agreed. Acceptance is Finance's sign-off on three consecutive daily tie-outs, so you decide when it is done.
Three consecutive days is reasonable and easy for my team to run.
Then the open point is payment. I want half on acceptance, not on signature.
Our norm would be half on signature, but we can agree half on acceptance and the balance 30 days after.
That works for me. Helena?
Then we have terms: 45 thousand fixed, three weeks after go-live, Finance sign-off, a credit if late, half on acceptance. Send the change request on Monday and I will sign it.

scene.title: Internal wrap-up
scene.goal: Capture decisions, owners and the message to the wider team

cases.condition: the team has assigned an owner and a next action for each follow-up

dialogue.text: That went better than I feared. Let us capture it: the change request goes out Monday, with the terms Helena repeated back to us.
I will draft and send the change request on Monday morning and call Priya to confirm. I will also tell our account lead the conversation ended in a good place.
There is also the ingestion risk review and the build plan. Someone needs to book the review and send the plan to the delivery lead.
Tech lead, please own both: book the risk review and send me the build plan.
I will book the risk review for ingestion and plan the build, and I will send the plan to the delivery lead by Wednesday.
Then we are set: the account manager owns the change request and the call to Priya, the tech lead owns the review and the plan, and I will check both on Thursday.
